newsitem.title: THAILAND: INTERVIEW-Thai PTT to focus new investment in Asia.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Thai PTT to focus new investment in Asia.

text.p: With nearly 30 oil firms competing in the crowded Thai market, state-owned Petroleum Authority of Thailand (PTT) said on Tuesday it was switching its investment focus to overseas projects.

Nuttachat Charuchinda, senior vice president of PTT International, told Reuters in an interview that his unit, established after a major restructuring at PTT last February, was now investing in several Asian countries.

"We're serious in investing in China, the Philippines, India, Malaysia, Vietnam, Cambodia, Burma and Laos in this order eventually. We would be interested in investing in retail oil business and LPG," he said.
He said that PTT's strategic overseas partners should have financial strength and should know the market well so that it would be easy for PTT to gain access into that particular foreign market.

"PTT International prefers to concentrate on downstream projects such as retail businesses abroad because we're strong in this field while at the same time it doesn't require huge investment," Nuttachat said.

Most recently PTT International entered into a joint venture investment worth $90 million to construct a liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) depot with a total capacity of 50,000 tonnes in the southeastern Chinese town of Shantuo.

Of the total stake in the Chinese venture, PTT International holds 20 percent, Thailand's major conglomerate Charoen Pokphand Group holds 50 percent and the remainder is held by local businessmen, he said.
Upon completion in 1999, the depot will buy refrigerated LPG from the Middle East to be consumed locally.
"China currently can produce five million tonnes of LPG per year and we expect by the year 2000 that demand for consumption will rise to between 8.0-9.0 million tonnes annually," Nuttachat said.
Three pressurised LPG depots worth $44 million will be built near the depot and they are scheduled to be completed in 2006.
Another major project was now unfolding in the Philippines.

"We've entered into a joint venture with the Coastal Aruba Refining Co N.V. to co-lease a 2.4-million-barrel oil depot at the Subic Bay and an oil finished depot with a total capacity of 450,000 barrels at the former Clark Air Base," Nuttachat said.
